newsitem.title: USA: Quaker Oats Q3 beverage income down.
newsitem.headline: Quaker Oats Q3 beverage income down.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said its third quarter total beverage operating income fell 43 percent to $34.0 million from $59.4 million.
Total beverage sales of $593.4 million were 11 percent below last year's $664.0 million.

U.S. and Canadian beverage operating income of $57.7 million, excluding a $16.6 million restructuring charge, was 15 percent below $67.9 million a year ago, despite an increase for Gatorade sports drink, the company said.
Quaker said Snapple beverage volumes declined 23 percent.
The drop in U.S. and Canadian beverage income was also due to a summer promotional campaign for Snapple, the company said.

U.S. and Canadian beverage sales of $512.6 million were nine percent below $563.8 million. Gatorade volumes dropped four percent, following a 17 percent increase last year. Compared with two years ago, which was a "more normal temperature summer," Quaker said Gatorade volume for this quarter was up 12 percent.
International beverages recorded an operating loss of $6.9 million, compared with a loss of $8.5 million a year ago.
International beverage sales of $80.8 million were 19 percent below $100.2 million, as volume declined 18 percent.

The sales decline reflects a strategic pullback of Snapple in international markets and a decline in licensee pre-mix sales in certain Asia/Pacific markets. Gatorade volumes in Latin America increased seven percent and non-licensee northern Asia markets more than doubled.
Quaker said Gatorade's 80 percent share of the North American sports beverage segment held up "remarkably well," given another season of tough competition.

"Clearly, the biggest challenge facing the company is Snapple's disappointing performance," William Smithburg, chairman, said in a statement. "The integrated sampling and advertising campaign that ended in mid-September generated some excitement behind the brand this summer, but we're still disappointed. We did not plan for a financial pay-back this season, but hope to regain momentum next year."
He said Quaker is setting up plans for Snapple for next season, focusing spending directly on innovation and execution at the distributor level.
"Our goal is to put a floor under Snapple," Smithburg said, adding the aim is to achieve a cash profit for Snapple in 1997.
